title: R4b — vwf.yaml format 28: the slim stack, capabilities from tasks, project folders and languages from bootstrap

keeps.pass: No hit, except a passage that names an earlier format as history (D23): plugins/vwf/skills/setup/references/format-lineage.md, the 27-to-28 migration step, and the history passages of plugins/vwf/assets/vwf-config.md; and the pack payload shape in plugins/vwf/assets/stack-adapter.md (D32). Each such hit is listed with its reason in the run report.

release_levels.reason: config_format 28 slims the project stack, drops the workspace harness and repo.stack other than its pin, and moves the project folder to bootstrap (blueprint_format 26); setup migrates every vwf repo.
stackgen reads services and deploy in place of backing_template and deploy_template.
The manual describes config_format 28 and its migration.

decisions.decision: How R4 splits.
decisions.ruling: Two plans, two formats: R4a is format 27; this plan, R4b, is format 28.

decisions.decision: The workspace harness block goes; bootstrap describe reports only the ports test:e2e and test:golden.
decisions.ruling: Derive from tasks (Recommended): a capability is present when its task exists; ports from bootstrap describe, the other names from mise tasks ls in the repo. No record in vwf.yaml.
decisions.rejected: Keep the non-port keys; ask bootstrap for more ports first.

decisions.decision: bootstrap has no per-tool projects list (ST2).
decisions.ruling: Bootstrap plan first: bootstrap R2d (docs/plans/2026-11-15-projects in bootstrap) adds [projects.<name>] with folder in repo.toml, a projects list per tool, found by detect, and a category per tool in describe. It ships in bootstrap 4.0.0.
decisions.rejected: Repo-wide for now; keep the keys in format 28.

decisions.decision: registry.yaml path duplicates bootstrap's project folder.
decisions.ruling: Move it in R4b (Recommended): the migration sets repo.projects.<name>.folder from registry path, path leaves registry.yaml (a blueprint_format bump), and every reader gets the folder with bootstrap config get.

decisions.decision: The values of backing_template and deploy_template.
decisions.ruling: Rename only (Recommended): backing_template → services, deploy_template → deploy; the slug values stay; R5 decides what an entry means without packs.

decisions.decision: What a language is in format 28.
decisions.ruling: The bootstrap tool name (Recommended): a language is a linked bootstrap tool of category languages (node, go, ...). stack-vocabulary.md and the readers use that name; the known/unknown check against a template's language_facts moves to R5 with the packs.
decisions.rejected: Map tool to token; defer languages to R5.

decisions.decision: How the 27 to 28 migration treats languages and package_manager.
decisions.ruling: Detect, then drop (Recommended): set repo.projects.<name>.folder from registry path; run bootstrap detect --json and, on the user's yes, detect --add --yes; report each project with no linked language tool, with the fix (bootstrap add tool <t>); then remove both keys.

decisions.decision: Stated by the planner, confirmed at the shape gate: the format 28 schema.
decisions.ruling:
projects.

.stack keeps template (until R5), frameworks, dependencies, services, deploy, os, note; it loses languages and package_manager. repo.stack keeps only template. The workspace harness block goes; projects.

.harness.health stays.

decisions.decision: Stated by the planner, confirmed at the shape gate: the language and package-manager read.
decisions.ruling: bootstrap describe --json, run in the repo that holds the project: the data.tools entries of category languages or package-managers whose projects list names the project.

decisions.decision: Stated by the planner, confirmed at the shape gate: the capability read.
decisions.ruling: A port capability is describe data.ports[].present; any other capability is a task name in mise tasks ls --json. harness.md maps each capability to its task name.

decisions.decision: Stated by the planner, confirmed at the shape gate: the registry.
decisions.ruling:
blueprint_format 26 and vwf_registry 3 remove path. A project's folder is bootstrap config get repo.projects..folder --json, run in its repo: projects.

.repo (R4a), else the base repo.

decisions.decision: Stated by the planner, confirmed at the shape gate: the 27 to 28 step, per repo.
decisions.ruling: Set the project folders (D4); detect (D7); report a project with no linked language tool; rename the two keys; remove languages, package_manager, repo.stack.package_manager, repo.stack.tools and harness; set config_format 28 and blueprint_format 26; run bootstrap sync --json; commit as R4a does (members first). A failed bootstrap call stops that repo's step with bootstrap's errors.

decisions.decision: Stated by the planner, confirmed at the shape gate: stackgen.
decisions.ruling: stackgen's readers use services and deploy. Pack data (a pack's languages: frontmatter, its package-manager facts) stays until R5.

decisions.decision: Stated by the planner, confirmed at the shape gate: the release levels.
decisions.ruling: vwf MAJOR, stackgen PATCH, site MINOR, installer NONE.

decisions.decision: Stated by the planner, confirmed at the shape gate: the gates.
decisions.ruling: The gates of R4a. K1 greps plugins/vwf/ for backing_template, deploy_template, package_manager, stack.languages and a top-level harness: key.

decisions.decision: Round 1 gap 1: plugins/vwf/assets/blueprint-format holds 25, and no unit owns it.
decisions.ruling: U1 owns it and sets it to 26.

decisions.decision: Round 1 gap 2: agents/architecture-writer.md writes the registry path and vwf_registry: 2, unowned.
decisions.ruling: U1 owns it; the agent writes no path and writes vwf_registry: 3.

decisions.decision: Round 1 gap 3: does the unknown-language rule stay now?
decisions.ruling: Remove the unknown-language rule (doctor lib/stack.mjs) and start.mjs --continue-unknown-language now: template tokens and bootstrap tool names cannot be compared. Doctor reports a project with no linked language tool as drift. The per-language walk uses the tool name. U3 also owns execute/workflows/folder.md and all.md.

decisions.decision: Round 1 gap 4: the task name of each capability, and the command.
decisions.ruling:
Fixed names: dev → dev; e2e_local → port test:e2e; local_stack → stack:up; e2e_staging → test:e2e:staging; goldens → port test:golden; test:load → test:load; screenshots → screenshots. health stays per project (projects.

.harness.health). The command is mise tasks ls --json --no-global --hidden (bootstrap R1b D27). A non-canonical name is no longer supported; the migration reports each one the old harness block recorded, so the user renames that task.

decisions.decision: Round 1 gap 5: the registry path is base-relative, the folder repo-relative.
decisions.ruling: Strip the holding member's folder prefix; a path equal to it becomes '.'. A path outside every repo stops that repo's step with a question. A name that is not kebab case stops the step with a report. An existing entry at another folder asks which to keep (R4a D3). An entry at the same folder under another name takes vwf's name: set the new name, move its tool links (config set tools.<t>.projects), then unset the old name.

decisions.decision: Round 1 gap 6: the iac rule resolves project.path from the base.
decisions.ruling: An iac project whose folder in its own repo is not '.' is not its own repo: that is the finding, with the same waiver.

decisions.decision: Round 1 gap 7: do the doctor tests run the real mise?
decisions.ruling: No: the tests stub mise on PATH, as bootstrap is stubbed.

decisions.decision: Round 2 gap 1: vwf-config.md history passages of formats 13, 15, 16 and 19 name the old keys; K1 and U1 have different exceptions.
decisions.ruling: K1 and U1 share one exception: a passage that names an earlier format as history is an allowed hit; the run report lists each one.

decisions.decision: Round 2 gap 2: which repo runs mise tasks ls and the describe port read.
decisions.ruling: The repo that holds the project whose platform needs the capability.

decisions.decision: Round 2 gap 3: a missing mise or a failed mise tasks ls; needsMise loses its harness input.
decisions.ruling: A failed mise call is a refusal, as a failed bootstrap call is. needsMise (doctor lib/stack.mjs) keys on the pins alone.

decisions.decision: Round 2 gap 4: a registry project with no repo.projects.<name>.
decisions.ruling: A drift row for that project, with the fix bootstrap config set repo.projects.<name> '{"folder":"<path>"}' --json; start.mjs skips that project.

decisions.decision: Round 2 gap 5: some projects have no language tool by nature.
decisions.ruling: No drift row when every platform of the project is iac, cicd or misc; the migration report (D12 step 3) skips them the same way.

decisions.decision: Round 3 gap 1: drift is not a doctor severity; rows use blocking, degraded and info.
decisions.ruling: The D18 row (no linked language tool) and the D26 row (no repo.projects.<name>) are both degraded. A degraded row never stops /vwf:execute.

decisions.decision: Round 3 gap 2: the JSON paths of bootstrap describe --json (data.tools shape, projects, ports) are not fixed by the bootstrap plans; a stub cannot catch a wrong path.
decisions.ruling: Before U4 writes code, it runs the real bootstrap describe --json (4.0.0, from the hand step) in a scratch repo, and records in its DECIDED line the exact paths of the tool category, the tool projects and the port presence. The stub copies that real shape.

decisions.decision: Round 3 gap 3: members migrate first; a failed member step still lets the base step remove the registry path, so a re-run loses that member's folders.
decisions.ruling: The base repo's step 6 and its stamps run only after every member step succeeds. If a member step fails, the base step stops too.

decisions.decision: Round 3 gap 4: /vwf:architecture runs config set repo.projects.<name> for a new project whose folder does not exist yet; bootstrap check then exits 2 (R2d D10).
decisions.ruling: Architecture writes the entry only when the folder exists. Otherwise the plan unit that creates the folder also runs the config set, and plan/references/delta-checks.md says so. Until then the D26 degraded row reports the missing entry.
decisions.rejected: Create the folder at architecture time.

decisions.decision: Round 4 gap 1: K1 flags package_manager: and harness: in the template payload block of stack-adapter.md; that is pack data that stays until R5 (D13).
decisions.ruling: K1 and U1 also excuse the pack payload shape in stack-adapter.md; the run report lists each excused line. R5 removes those keys.

decisions.decision: Round 4 gap 2: the migration meets a registry project whose path folder does not exist yet.
decisions.ruling: Step 1 skips the config set for that project; the migration report shows the fix line bootstrap config set repo.projects.<name> '{"folder":"<path>"}' --json. The D26 degraded row reports the missing entry until the folder exists.

decisions.decision: Round 4 gap 3: under D30 a member repo absent on this machine can never complete its step.
decisions.ruling: An absent member stops the migration with a report that names the member to clone. The base repo stays at format 27 until that member is present.

decisions.decision: Amended 2026-11-22: start.mjs refused the plan, because review row U6 did not cover every earlier wave-1 unit (the rule that a review row's coverage and its commit range agree).
decisions.ruling: U6 depends_on is widened to every wave-1 unit (U1 to U5). The prose units are covered so that coverage and range agree; the wave review already judged them, so the review focus does not change.
decisions.rejected: Move the prose units to a wave after U6, with a second review row after them.

decisions.decision: Q1: In the 27-to-28 migration, should /vwf:setup stop when a pinned project has no linked bootstrap language tool?
decisions.ruling: No — setup reports a pinned project with no linked bootstrap language tool like any degraded row and continues.
decisions.rejected: Yes — setup halts and reverts the stamp, as the old unknown-language halt did

decisions.decision: Q2: Should doctor checks.mjs emit any capability rows from the D10/D19 read (describe ports + mise tasks ls), and if so which?
decisions.ruling: A degraded harness row for the capabilities a platform implies (dev, screenshots, goldens) — adds a mise call, stubbed in the tests.
decisions.rejected: None; doctor capability section stays prose-only; A row for every harness.md capability — needs blueprint reads in the script

decisions.decision: Q3: When mise is not on PATH and a project has a screen platform, should doctor checks.mjs refuse (D25) or skip the D37 capability read?
decisions.ruling: Refuse, as D25 says for a failed mise call — keep what U4 built; doctor stops, and the missing-mise row never appears.
decisions.rejected: Skip the capability read when mise is not on PATH — doctor still runs and its existing mise row reports the missing tool
